items.title: Make evaluateReviewEscalation freshness-root gitCwd-aware
items.context: packages/main/src/core/review-escalation.ts ~439-440: add gitCwd?: string to EvaluateReviewEscalationArgs, compute const gitCwd = args.gitCwd ?? args.projectRoot, and change currentMaterialHash(args.projectRoot)/currentStoryFilesHash(args.projectRoot) to currentMaterialHash(gitCwd,'HEAD',args.projectRoot)/currentStoryFilesHash(gitCwd,'HEAD',args.projectRoot), matching review-assurance-floor.ts:439 and producers (quorum-submit.ts:247/251, verifier.ts:610).

happy.desc: After adding gitCwd? to EvaluateReviewEscalationArgs and changing lines 439-440 to use const gitCwd = args.gitCwd ?? args.projectRoot with currentMaterialHash(gitCwd,"HEAD",args.projectRoot)/currentStoryFilesHash(gitCwd,"HEAD",args.projectRoot): call evaluateReviewEscalation with gitCwd pointing at the inner git root in a wrapper-root layout -> materialHash and storyFilesHash in the returned report match the values produced by evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor with the same gitCwd. WHY: proves the core fix aligns the freshness-root computation.

In a plain repo (gitCwd === projectRoot), call evaluateReviewEscalation with and without the gitCwd field -> both produce identical materialHash/storyFilesHash. WHY: confirms backward compatibility (no-op when gitCwd is absent or equals projectRoot).

edge.desc: Call evaluateReviewEscalation where args.materialHash and args.storyFilesHash are explicitly supplied (pre-computed) -> the function uses the supplied values and never calls currentMaterialHash/currentStoryFilesHash at all (same as before). WHY: verifies the ?? short-circuit on line 439 means callers like quorum-submit that pass explicit hashes are unaffected by the gitCwd plumbing.

Call evaluateReviewEscalation with gitCwd pointing to a directory that is NOT the projectRoot and NOT a git repo -> falls back gracefully (materialHash/storyFilesHash are null) without throwing. WHY: wrapper-root edge where gitCwd resolution might fail.

adversarial.desc: In a wrapper-root layout, call evaluateReviewEscalation WITHOUT gitCwd (old behavior, using only projectRoot where projectRoot is the non-git metadata root) -> materialHash is null or differs from what evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor produces with the correct gitCwd. WHY: red-documents the bug by proving the old code path diverges, validating that the fix is necessary.

items.userSees: Running `node packages/main/dist/tasks/review-escalation-smoke.js` still prints its existing pass line and `npm --prefix packages/main run build` succeeds with the new gitCwd? arg on EvaluateReviewEscalationArgs.

verificationEvidence.note: WRAPPER case asserts floor.materialHash===escalation.materialHash and ===currentMaterialHash(repoDir,HEAD,metaRoot) with gitCwd=inner repo — proves the core fix aligns the freshness root.
PLAIN no-change regression: escalation with gitCwd and without gitCwd yields identical materialHash/storyFilesHash (gitCwd defaults to projectRoot).

Lines 439-440 keep the `args.materialHash ?? ...` / `args.storyFilesHash ?? ...` short-circuit, so callers supplying explicit hashes (e.g. quorum-submit:329) never invoke currentMaterialHash/currentStoryFilesHash; the gitCwd plumbing cannot affect them.

WRAPPER RED path runs the freshness probe from a non-git dir (gitCwd defaults to the non-git metaRoot): currentMaterialHash returns undefined and the evaluator yields null WITHOUT throwing — the same graceful git-failure fallback for any non-git gitCwd.
WRAPPER RED assertion: escalation WITHOUT gitCwd (projectRoot=non-git metaRoot) -> materialHash null and !== floor.materialHash, red-documenting the pre-fix divergence.

items.title: Plumb resolved gitCwd into the DONE-gate escalation calls
items.context: Pass escalation the SAME resolved gitCwd as the adjacent evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor: done-oracle.ts ~751 (gitCwd already in scope at :787), machine.ts ~639 (context.gitCwd ?? resolveGitCwd{...}, mirroring :648) and ~1140 (gitCwd ?? resolveGitCwd{...}, mirroring :1151). Byte-identical in plain repos.

happy.desc: In done-oracle.ts ~751: after plumbing gitCwd into evaluateReviewEscalation({projectRoot: root, storyId, store, gitCwd}), run buildDoneChecklist under a wrapper-root layout where gitCwd != root -> the review-escalation row and the review-assurance-floor row report the SAME materialHash. WHY: proves the DONE-gate escalation call now agrees with the adjacent floor call (line 785-788 already passes gitCwd).

In machine.ts ~639: after plumbing gitCwd into evaluateReviewEscalation({projectRoot: context.projectRoot, storyId: context.storyId, store: context.store, gitCwd: context.gitCwd ?? resolveGitCwd(...)}), invoke the DONE-readiness path in StoryMachine under a wrapper-root layout -> escalation.materialHash === floor.materialHash. WHY: proves the machine.ts caller at ~639 threads the same gitCwd as the floor at ~648.

In machine.ts ~1140: after plumbing gitCwd into the second evaluateReviewEscalation call, invoke the DONE-gate transition path under a wrapper-root layout -> escalation.materialHash === floor.materialHash at ~1149. WHY: proves both machine.ts call sites are fixed.

edge.desc: In done-oracle.ts and machine.ts, when gitCwd is not provided (options.gitCwd absent), escalation falls back to projectRoot (root) for hash computation, producing the same result as before -> no regression in plain repos. WHY: confirms the fallback path (gitCwd ?? root) is byte-identical to the pre-fix behavior for plain repos.

adversarial.desc: In machine.ts ~639, omit gitCwd from the evaluateReviewEscalation call while the adjacent evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor at ~646 passes gitCwd under a wrapper-root layout -> escalation.materialHash diverges from floor.materialHash, demonstrating the DONE gate would silently accept stale escalation data. WHY: red-documents that the plumbing is structurally required.

items.userSees: Running `node packages/main/dist/tasks/done-oracle-wrapper-root-smoke.js` passes; in a wrapper-root project the DONE checklist Review-escalation row uses the same resolved gitCwd as the Review-assurance-floor row (no false stale).

verificationEvidence.note: buildDoneChecklist passes under wrapper-root; done-oracle.ts:751 now threads the in-scope gitCwd already used by the adjacent floor row (:785-788). Evaluator-level floor==escalation equivalence proven by review-escalation-freshness-root-smoke.

GENUINE guard (F-003 fix): DONE-ready wrapper-root fixture (PASS test-evidence + signed delivery-check + escalation-required policy + 3x2 host verdicts bound to currentMaterialHash(gitRoot)) makes canFinishGuard(machine.ts:639) DEPEND on escalation reading the resolved gitCwd. Asserts canFinishGuard({gitCwd:gitRoot})===true; revert-proven: removing the gitCwd from machine.ts:639 makes the smoke FAIL (canFinishGuard false!==true).

GENUINE guard (F-003 fix): in the same DONE-ready wrapper-root fixture, asserts getGuardFailureReason(storyId,store,'DONE',metaRoot,gitRoot)===null (machine.ts:1145) and buildDoneChecklist review-escalation row status==='pass' with gitRoot vs 'fail' with metaRoot (done-oracle.ts:751). Reverting the escalation gitCwd plumbing flips these, so the call sites are genuinely guarded.
PLAIN no-change regression proves the `gitCwd ?? projectRoot` fallback is byte-identical for plain repos; resolveGitCwd also returns projectRoot when unresolved.

Red-documented by the new smoke WRAPPER RED (escalation without gitCwd -> null/diverges). Structurally, the floor at :646/:1149 passes gitCwd while pre-fix escalation did not, so the DONE gate would have compared divergent hashes.

items.title: Plumb gitCwd into the diagnostic escalation handlers
items.context: packages/main/src/handlers/review-escalation.ts review_escalation_status/policy_set/fallback_set: pass gitCwd via resolveGitCwd({store: ctx.store, storyId, metadataRoot: ctx.root, projectRoot: ctx.root}). Confirm quorum-submit.ts:329 already passes explicit materialHash/storyFilesHash so the internal recompute is bypassed (no change).

happy.desc: In handlers/review-escalation.ts review_escalation_status (~64): after adding gitCwd via resolveGitCwd({store: ctx.store, storyId: args.storyId, metadataRoot: ctx.root, projectRoot: ctx.root}), invoke the handler under a wrapper-root layout -> the returned report.materialHash matches the value from evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor with the same gitCwd. WHY: proves the diagnostic status handler is gitCwd-aware.

In handlers/review-escalation.ts review_escalation_policy_set (~126): after plumbing gitCwd, invoke the handler -> the embedded escalation report.materialHash agrees with the floor. WHY: the policy_set re-evaluates escalation after recording a policy event; its hash must match.

In handlers/review-escalation.ts review_escalation_fallback_set (~216): after plumbing gitCwd, invoke the handler -> the embedded escalation report.materialHash agrees with the floor. WHY: the fallback_set re-evaluates escalation; its hash must also match.

Confirm quorum-submit.ts line 329-335 already passes explicit materialHash and storyFilesHash to evaluateReviewEscalation, bypassing the internal currentMaterialHash/currentStoryFilesHash fallback -> no code change needed in quorum-submit.ts. WHY: verifies the checklist context assertion that the quorum path is unaffected.

edge.desc: In fallback_set handler, currentMaterialHash at line 181 and currentStoryFilesHash at line 189 are called with ctx.root (not gitCwd) for the FRESHNESS CHECK of the user-supplied materialHash -> verify whether these also need gitCwd. If ctx.root is the metadata root in a wrapper-root layout, these freshness checks would compute wrong hashes. WHY: potential secondary bug in the same handler that CHK-003 touches.

adversarial.desc: Call review_escalation_status handler WITHOUT gitCwd plumbing under a wrapper-root layout -> the returned report.materialHash is null or diverges from the floor, proving the diagnostic handler was also affected by the original bug. WHY: red-documents that handler-level plumbing is necessary, not just core+DONE-gate.

items.userSees: Running `node packages/main/dist/tasks/review-escalation-smoke.js` passes; `lattice review_escalation_status` and policy/fallback_set compute freshness from the resolved gitCwd instead of the metadata root.

verificationEvidence.note: WRAPPER-ROOT real-StoryStore case directly invokes createReviewEscalationHandlers(ctx).review_escalation_status({storyId}); asserts report.materialHash===floor and report.storyFilesHash===floorStory (currentMaterial/StoryFilesHash(gitRoot,HEAD,metaRoot)).
WRAPPER-ROOT real-StoryStore case directly invokes review_escalation_policy_set(...) and asserts the embedded report.materialHash===floor — direct handler runtime invocation under wrapper-root.

WRAPPER-ROOT real-StoryStore case directly invokes review_escalation_fallback_set(...) and asserts the embedded report.materialHash===floor — direct handler runtime invocation, also exercising the gitCwd-aware fallback freshness probe.
quorum-submit.ts:329-335 passes explicit materialHash+storyFilesHash to evaluateReviewEscalation, bypassing the internal recompute; left unchanged (the commit diff shows no quorum-submit edit).

Secondary same-class bug confirmed and FIXED: fallback_set freshness probes (:184 currentMaterialHash, :195 currentStoryFilesHash) and policy_set (:88/:90 currentMaterialHash/currentGitHead) now use the resolved gitCwd instead of ctx.root; byte-identical in plain repos.

Red-documented by the new smoke WRAPPER RED (evaluator without gitCwd -> null/diverges); the handlers previously called the evaluator with projectRoot only, so the diagnostic was affected identically.

items.title: Add offline floor<->escalation freshness-root equivalence smoke + plain-repo regression
items.context: New packages/main/src/tasks/review-escalation-freshness-root-smoke.ts: under BOTH plain and wrapper-root layouts assert floor.materialHash === escalation.materialHash and escalation.{materialHash,storyFilesHash} === currentMaterialHash/currentStoryFilesHash(gitCwd,'HEAD',projectRoot); add a RED-documenting assertion that escalation without gitCwd diverges (null) in wrapper-root, plus a plain-repo no-change regression. Wire an npm script and into the npm test chain.

happy.desc: New smoke test under plain-repo layout: call evaluateReviewAssuranceFloor and evaluateReviewEscalation with the same (gitCwd === projectRoot) and assert floor.materialHash === escalation.materialHash and escalation.materialHash === currentMaterialHash(gitCwd,"HEAD",projectRoot). WHY: plain-repo no-change regression proving floor<->escalation equivalence in the common case.

New smoke test under wrapper-root layout (git root != metadata/project root): set up a temporary wrapper-root where metadataRoot is a non-git parent and gitCwd is the inner git root, call both evaluators with the same gitCwd -> floor.materialHash === escalation.materialHash and both equal currentMaterialHash(gitCwd,"HEAD",projectRoot). WHY: proves wrapper-root equivalence end-to-end.

Smoke test is wired into npm test chain (npm script entry) and passes in CI -> ensures the equivalence assertion runs on every build. WHY: prevents future regressions from breaking the floor<->escalation alignment.

edge.desc: Smoke test covers storyFilesHash equivalence in addition to materialHash: under both plain and wrapper-root layouts assert escalation.storyFilesHash === currentStoryFilesHash(gitCwd,"HEAD",projectRoot). WHY: the bug affects both hashes (lines 439 and 440); both must be tested.

Smoke test handles the case where the story has no findings and escalation is not required -> escalation still reports correct materialHash/storyFilesHash even when ok=true and required=false. WHY: most stories do not trigger escalation but must still compute correct hashes for the report.

adversarial.desc: RED-documenting assertion in the smoke test: under wrapper-root layout, call evaluateReviewEscalation WITHOUT gitCwd (only projectRoot = metadataRoot) -> assert materialHash is null or diverges from floor.materialHash, and storyFilesHash is null or diverges from floor.storyFilesHash. WHY: proves that omitting gitCwd in wrapper-root causes the exact divergence the bug describes; the test documents the failure mode and would catch if the fix were reverted.

Plain-repo regression assertion: run the smoke test against a plain repo where gitCwd === projectRoot and confirm that the old code path (no gitCwd field) and the new code path (gitCwd = projectRoot) produce byte-identical results -> no behavioral change for plain repos. WHY: guards against the fix accidentally changing plain-repo semantics.

items.userSees: Running `node packages/main/dist/tasks/review-escalation-freshness-root-smoke.js` prints `review-escalation freshness-root smoke passed`, and `npm test` runs test:review-escalation-freshness-root green.

verificationEvidence.note: PLAIN case asserts floor.materialHash===escalation.materialHash===currentMaterialHash(root,HEAD,root).
WRAPPER case (non-git metaRoot + inner gitRoot) asserts floor==escalation==currentMaterialHash(repoDir,HEAD,metaRoot) end-to-end.
New smoke wired into the root test chain (test:review-escalation-freshness-root inserted after test:done-escalation-drift-advisory); `npm test` exited 0 with the new script executed.
Both PLAIN and WRAPPER cases assert escalation.storyFilesHash===currentStoryFilesHash(gitCwd,HEAD,projectRoot) (line 440 of the fix), covering the storyFilesHash hash in addition to materialHash.
Story uses findings:[] so escalation.required=false/ok=true, yet materialHash/storyFilesHash are still computed and asserted (the evaluator computes both before the required branch).
WRAPPER RED assertion: without gitCwd, materialHash is null and !== floor.materialHash — would catch a revert of the core fix.
PLAIN regression: escalation with gitCwd=projectRoot vs without the gitCwd field -> byte-identical materialHash/storyFilesHash, guarding against accidental plain-repo behavior change.
